tool_args.rationale: The pilot and acquired rows show a smooth concave response to u_now plus a strong decrease at high s_grad. The open-branch measurement provided the required gradient span; fit the simplest documented siphon law with a free signed sqrt branch term to all seven paid observations.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Already acquired; its low- and high-gradient observations establish a large sink effect and inform the signed branch fit.
All observed rows share H, x_now, and memory conditions; no trajectory evidence indicates a coupled dynamic mechanism, and this probe is unnecessary for the parsimonious static law.

The rows all use H=0.6, so horizon dependence is not identifiable, but the observed sink-gradient contrast and supplied pilot signatures directly support the static sink-inhibited family; no slow-horizon probe is currently justified.
It adds a barrier-activation parameter without evidence requiring that added curvature; the simpler siphon-with-signed-branch model is the more economical working hypothesis.
It is unrelated to resolving the observed response structure and is explicitly not useful here.
